english: Let $A=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ and $B=\{1,2,3,4\}$. Consider the set $T$ of all functions $f:A\to B$ such that $f(i)\neq i$ for every $i\in B$. Among the elements of $T$, exactly $p$ functions have a one-one restriction to $B$, and exactly $q$ functions are onto. Then the value of $p-q$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ तथा $B=\{1,2,3,4\}$ है। उन सभी फलनों $f:A\to B$ के समुच्चय $T$ पर विचार कीजिए जिनके लिए प्रत्येक $i\in B$ हेतु $f(i)\neq i$ है। $T$ के अवयवों में से ठीक $p$ फलनों का $B$ पर प्रतिबन्ध एकैकी है, तथा ठीक $q$ फलन आच्छादक हैं। तब $p-q$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $p$: $f|_B:B\to B$ one-one means a bijection of $B$ with no $f(i)=i$: a derangement of $4$ objects, $D_4=9$; $f(5)$ is free ($4$ ways), so $p=36$
Every such $f$ is onto (already $f(B)=B$), so these $36$ are among the $q$ onto functions
$q$ by inclusion-exclusion on the values missed: if a set $K\subseteq B$ of $k$ values is avoided, each $i\in B\setminus K$ has $3-k$ choices, each $i\in K$ and $5$ have $4-k$ choices
solution_full: Count $p$. The restriction $f|_B$ maps $B$ into $B$; it is one-one on a finite set of the same size, so it is a bijection of $B$, and $f(i)\neq i$ for all $i\in B$ makes it a derangement of $4$ objects: $D_4=4!\left(1-1+\dfrac12-\dfrac16+\dfrac1{24}\right)=9$. The value $f(5)\in B$ is unrestricted ($4$ ways), so $p=9\cdot4=36$.

Each of these $36$ functions already has $f(B)=B$, so its range equals the codomain and it is onto. The remaining onto functions are those where $f|_B$ is many-one and $f(5)$ supplies the missing value.
Count $q$ directly by inclusion-exclusion over the values of $B$ that are not attained. Fix a set $K\subseteq B$ of $k$ values that $f$ avoids. Then $f$ maps into $B\setminus K$ ($4-k$ values).

An element $i\in B\setminus K$ must avoid itself as well, so it has $3-k$ choices; an element $i\in K$ has all $4-k$ choices (its forbidden value $i$ is already excluded); the element $5$ has $4-k$ choices.
Check: $q-p=48$ onto functions have $f|_B$ with exactly three values and $f(5)$ equal to the fourth value.
originality_note: New: inside the family of functions A -> B with no fixed point on B, one-one-ness of the restriction to B forces onto, so the onto count splits into a derangement part and a part where the extra element 5 completes the range (way 5). Closest known: counting onto functions from a 5-set to a 4-set (240) and derangements. Different because: the fixed-point condition changes the inclusion-exclusion weights (elements in K have one more choice than elements outside K), and the student must see that p counts a subset of the onto functions.
blueprint_concepts: One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horizontal line and algebraic tests
Onto vs into: comparing range with codomain
Number of one-one and onto functions between finite sets

concept_use.One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horiz: The restriction f|_B is one-one from B to B, hence a bijection of B; with f(i) != i it is a derangement, giving p = 9 x 4.
concept_use.Onto vs into: comparing range with codom: f is onto when its range equals the codomain B; one-one f|_B already gives range B, and otherwise f(5) must supply the missing value.
concept_use.Number of one-one and onto functions bet: q = 84 by inclusion-exclusion over the avoided values, N_k = (3-k)^(4-k)(4-k)^(k+1), and p = D_4 x 4 = 36.

stem_review: Read as a student: A, B, T, the restriction and both counts are defined; the condition f(i) != i applies only to i in B (5 is not in B), stated as 'for every i in B'; p = 36, q = 84 and p - q = -48 verified by brute force over all 1024 functions; matches the plan 'negative integer'. Changed: rephrased the definitions of T, p and q ('Consider the set T ...', 'exactly p functions ...') so the stem lint does not read p, q as functions; meaning unchanged.
key_step: Inclusion-exclusion with the fixed-point restriction: N_k = (3-k)^(4-k)(4-k)^(k+1), giving q = 84; p = D_4 x 4 = 36.
justification: Two counting ideas linked (derangements and onto counting by inclusion-exclusion with modified weights), with a precise final number and no options; one slip in the weights changes the answer. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q11 (L3), a bounded-distribution count, and below 2026-P2-Q10 (L4), which hides the one-one condition more deeply.
